version.changelog: 移除PROXY_TOKEN硬编码，修复安全网关T09拦截问题

llm.summary: This hotel-search skill discloses that it sends query data to a cloud proxy and I found no hidden persistence, local data access, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: Outbound network use and a proxy token are proportionate for real-time hotel search, but users should trust the configured proxy before sending travel queries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency bootstrap, package download, or setup-time execution was found; the script uses Python standard library modules.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The user-facing tools are narrow, but the exact proxy origin is supplied externally through PROXY_URL rather than declared as a fixed allowlisted endpoint.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No file writes, subprocess or shell execution, scheduled tasks, memory modification, privilege escalation, or local credential/profile access was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Courtyard by Marriott hotel search, details, packages, prices, and booking links; SKILL.md and the Python script match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending hotel destinations, dates, hotel names, and related search terms to the configured proxy and travel platform. Make sure PROXY_URL and PROXY_TOKEN are provisioned by a trusted source, and do not treat the returned booking links as completed reservations until you review the external booking page.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Confirmed: the script posts hotel-query parameters and X-Proxy-Token to PROXY_URL. This is consistent with the disclosed proxy data flow, though configuration should come from a trusted source.
[LP3] expected: Partly confirmed: SKILL.md declares the hotel tools and data flow but does not name or constrain the proxy endpoint. This is a scoping/documentation note, not evidence of hidden behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: Confirmed Chinese-only presentation. The skill metadata, examples, and hotel-search domain are also Chinese-facing, so this is not a security concern for this artifact.
[SQP-2] expected: Confirmed: user search terms can be sent off-box. SKILL.md explicitly documents user input flowing through the skill to a cloud proxy and travel platform API.
